To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the human cellular src gene has a nucleotide sequence very highly conserved with respect both to the chicken cellular src gene and to the Rous sarcomaviral src gene, and that the amino acid sequence of human pp60c-src is very highly conserved between humans and chickens, with 98% amino acid identity between the two proteins.

the human c-src sequence has been determined, and that the amino acid sequence of this gene is strongly conserved with the c-src genes of chickens and the v-src gene of Rous sarcoma viruses, and that this conservation is greatest in the tyrosine protein kinase domain of the protein.

the human src gene is highly conserved with respect both to the chicken src gene and to the Rous sarcomavirus src gene, and that the human src protein is highly conserved in the carboxy terminal two-thirds of its sequence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular biology of the cellular src gene.
the molecular biology of the cellular src gene.
the isolation, characterization, and expression of the cellular src genes of various animal species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the amino acid sequences of the tyrosine protein kinases of human c-src and chicken c-src are identical.
the src genes of human and chicken are highly conserved at both the nucleotide and amino acid levels.
the human c-src sequence reported herein has a high degree of homology with both the chicken and the Rous virus c-src sequences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this portion of human cellular src is very highly conserved, with 90% homology at the nucleotide level and 98% homology at amino acid level.
the human cellular src gene has been cloned and sequenced, and it is very highly conserved with respect both to chicken c-src and to Rous sarcoma viral v-src.
we have cloned a 3.2-kilobase pair (kbp) human cDNA clone that codes for the carboxyl-terminal two-thirds of the pp60v-src protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amino acid sequence is very strongly homologous between human and chicken.
we have a better idea of the structure of the protein, and we have a better understanding of the structure of its binding site.
we have identified an important functional domain in pp60c-src that may be involved in cellular transformation by Rous sarcoma viruses.
